$schema.description: A URL to the JSON Schema for this object.

carried_from_id.description: Optional. Finding id in the previous report this continues

description.description: Required. Plain text for a reader in a hurry: blank lines separate short paragraphs, lines starting with '- ' are bullets, backticks mark code, files, functions and errors. No paragraph over 600 characters; three or four blocks at most

evidence.description: Recommended. What established the finding beyond reading the code

expected.description: Recommended. What the code is supposed to guarantee here, the groundwork the steps break. Same shape as description; follows normal use on the chain

exploit_path.description: Optional. Shown only to verified owners

exploit_path_withheld.description: An exploit path exists on this finding but is shown only to verified owners

exploitable_by.description: Recommended. The privilege an attacker needs to reach this finding, from least to most: anyone (no account, no session), any_user (any signed-in account) or any_signer (any funded key), account_owner (a member of the affected account or position), api_key (an integration's credentials), internal_network (inside the network or a VPN), admin (a privileged role), upgrade_authority (the platform operator or upgrade key), other_program (only through another program or service), internal (insider standing on the code or the telemetry: repo, snapshot or store access, never a customer), none. Shown to every reader

fix.description: Required. A '- ' bullet per change. A code fence (three backticks on their own line, closed the same way) right after a bullet carries the definite fix: the correct code, the exact header value, the configuration line. A fence whose info line names a place, like rust src/lib.rs:41-45, is shown as a patch replacing those lines (path:line alone inserts before it)

fix_kind.description: Optional. operational says there are no lines to patch (rotate, revoke, configure), so the dry run stops advising a placed fence for a finding that names a file

fix_sites.description: Server-captured code for every fix fence that names a location; the page renders such a fence as a patch against these lines

id.description: Server-assigned finding id, present on stored reports

impact.description: Recommended. What the finding costs when it happens: who loses what, in plain terms. Same shape as description; the last item of the reproduction chain, carrying the finding-level attachments

normal_use.description: Recommended. How this code is ordinarily used: who calls it, with what, and what comes back. Same shape as description; the first item of the reproduction chain

severity_changes.description: Server-kept history of re-ratings, oldest first; severity is the current rating. Ignored when posted

sites.description: Recommended for critical and high. Further places this finding points at, in order

sites_kind.description: Recommended with sites. How the sites relate; required when sites are present

snippet.description: The enclosing item at the location

status.description: Optional, defaults to open. Set by the owner afterwards; archived means judged not relevant, with a reason on status_changes, and is not counted

status_changes.description: Server-kept history of status moves, oldest first, archiving with its reason. Ignored when posted

visuals.description: Optional. Attachments for the finding as a whole, shown on the impact item: the script that ran it, a recording, a dump. Served from the stored bytes by id. A finding carries one recording in all, here or on a step
